name: Wade Hampton Frost
summary: American epidemiologist who established the first dedicated department of epidemiology at Johns Hopkins.

name: Lowell Reed
summary: American biostatistician and population ecologist who collaborated with Frost on epidemic theory.

name: Johns Hopkins School of Hygiene
summary: Academic institution where the first department of epidemiology was established.

name: Department of Epidemiology
aliases: department of epidemiology at the Hopkins School for Hygiene
summary: First dedicated academic department of epidemiology, chaired by Frost.

name: Department of Biometry and Vital Statistics
aliases: department for biometry and vital statistics
summary: Department established by Reed focusing on mathematical analysis of health data.

name: Harvard University
summary: University where Frost delivered a key lecture on epidemic theory in 1928.

name: Reed-Frost epidemic theory
summary: Mechanical model using marbles and a trough to simulate epidemic dynamics.

name: Baltimore
summary: City where Johns Hopkins University is located and where students conducted fieldwork.

name: United States
summary: Country where Frost and Reed worked and epidemiology was institutionalized.

name: United Kingdom
summary: Country where epidemiological societies advanced thinking prior to US institutionalization.

name: Raymond Pearl
summary: Epidemiologist who brought Pearson's biometric school of thought to the US.

name: Karl Pearson
summary: Statistician whose methods influenced the mathematical rigor of epidemiology.

name: Brian MacMahon
summary: Epidemiologist who introduced the 'web of causation' concept in textbooks.

name: Thomas Pugh
summary: Epidemiologist who co-authored textbooks on epidemiological principles.

name: Philip Fine
summary: Epidemiologist who published a commentary on the Reed-Frost model in 1977.

name: Helen Abbey
summary: Researcher who interpreted the mathematical theory of Reed and Frost.
